citation_convention: pN = PDF page index N (1-based). Printed page number = N for N = 1..36; PDF p37 is printed page 38 (printed page 37 is absent); PDF p38-p48 are the unnumbered package addendum, packaging, mechanical and legal pages. Types: TYP = typical table value at 25 C; MIN/MAX = guaranteed limit at 25 C ('ensured by testing or statistical analysis', p5 note 2) unless marked 'over temp' (-40 C <= TJ <= +125 C); CURVE = read from a typical-characteristic plot by sampling the vector paths of the PDF drawing (pdf_vector_paths_sampler.py), axis calibration checked on the rendered figure; SIM = stated as a simulation result; TEXT = value stated in prose or application text, not in a specification table; DERIVED = computed here from datasheet data (formula given).
input_type: bipolar (TI SiGe process, p1; input bias current about -15 uA, p6). The datasheet does not name the input-stage device type explicitly.
compensation: selectable (WSON-8 only): COMP pin LO or open (internal pull-down, default) = maximum internal compensation, minimum stable gain 4 V/V, GBWP 1.7 GHz (TEXT p33); COMP pin HI = reduced compensation, minimum stable gain 10 V/V, GBWP 4 GHz (TEXT p29, p31, p34). SOT-23-5 has no COMP pin and is internally fixed at a minimum stable gain of 10 V/V (p1, p20). Decompensated in both settings.

min_stable_gain.conditions: COMP LO: 'on-chip compensation is set to the maximum and bandwidth is reduced to enable stability at gains as low as 4V/V'. COMP HI: 'minimum stable gain is 10V/V. Due to the reduced compensation, slew rate and large signal bandwidth are significantly enhanced for the higher gains' (p20). p31: choose SOT23-5 'if Power Down is not needed and closed loop gain is >= 20dB'.
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: External compensation (p20-p22, Fig 50): a series Rc-Cc network between the two inputs raises the noise gain at high frequency. Constraint 1: (1 + Rf/Rg)(1 + (Rp + REQ)/Rc) >= 10 V/V (may be changed to >= 4 V/V for WSON-8 with COMP LO); Constraint 2: 1/(2 pi Cc Rc) <= 90 MHz; Rp = Rs||RT (non-inverting) and REQ = Rf||Rg. Reasons listed: SOT-23-5 at closed-loop gain < 10 V/V; WSON-8 below 4 V/V with COMP LO; either package at low gain when maximum slew rate (COMP HI) is wanted. Worked example (SOT-23-5, +3.7 V/V): Rf = 249 ohm, Rg = 91 ohm, REQ = 66.6 ohm, Rs = RT = 50 ohm (Rp = 25 ohm), Rc ~ 56 ohm, Cc ~ 33 pF; measured response Fig 51 '-3 dB response of about 1 GHz' (with Cf' = 1.5 pF across Rf through a T network RA = 33 ohm, RB = 91 ohm, needed for the SOT-23-5 summing-node capacitance; 'The WSON-8 package does not need this compensation across Rf due to its lower parasitics'). The Rc-Cc network lowers the input impedance (-3 dB at 490 MHz) and raises the noise gain (Eq 1: noise-gain zero 1/(2 pi (Rc + Rp + REQ) Cc), 3 dB increase at 32.8 MHz for these values). TIA (p28-p29): no explicit minimum-gain statement; Fig 61 shows the high-frequency noise gain 1 + C_IN/C_F, and the text recommends COMP HI (or SOT-23) for maximum speed in the TIA.

packages.name: WSON-8 (NGQ0008A)
packages.ep_connection: DAP tied to V- inside the package; must be soldered to the board; board copper connected to it must be at V- (p19); 'thermal pad must be soldered to the printed circuit board for thermal and mechanical performance' (p45 note 3)
packages.notes: Only package with PD, COMP and FB pins. Land pattern p46: pins 0.6 x 0.25 mm, 2.8 mm row pitch, thermal pad 1.6 x 2 mm with 0.2 mm vias; stencil 0.1 mm, 82 % paste coverage on pad 9 (p47). MSL 3 / 260 C. Orderables LMH6629SD/NOPB (1000), SDE (250), SDX (4500), marking L6629.

packages.name: SOT-23-5 (DBV0005A)
packages.notes: No PD, COMP or FB pin; fixed minimum gain 10 V/V; higher SSBW with more peaking than WSON-8 (p20). MSL 1. Orderables LMH6629MF/NOPB (1000), MFE (250), MFX (3000), marking AE7A.

pinout_notes: WSON-8 (NGQ): 1 PD (power down, active low, floats high = on), 2 FB (feedback, internally connected to OUT, lets RF sit next to IN-), 3 IN-, 4 IN+, 5 V-, 6 COMP (internal pull-down; LO = min gain 4, HI = min gain 10), 7 OUT, 8 V+, DAP = V-. SOT-23-5 (DBV): 1 OUT, 2 V-, 3 +IN, 4 -IN, 5 V+. Logic thresholds (PD and COMP, single-supply tables, i.e. relative to V- = ground): VIL 0.8 V max, VIH 2.5 V min (5 V) / 2.0 V min (3.3 V); logic input current about -28 uA (LO) and -22 uA (HI) TYP (flows out). Enable 75 ns, disable 80 ns; in shutdown the output stage is high impedance (feedback network sets output impedance). (p3, p7, p10, p19, p20)

tia_content.other: Eq 8: C_F = sqrt(C_IN / (2 pi GBWP R_F)); Eq 9: f_-3dB ~ sqrt(GBWP / (2 pi R_F C_IN)). 'This C_F value is a starting point and C_F needs to be tuned for the particular application as it is often less than 1 pF and thus is easily affected by board parasitics. For maximum speed, the LMH6629 COMP pin should be HI (or use the SOT-23 package).' DERIVED check: C_IN = 10 + 1.7 + 4 = 15.7 pF gives f_-3dB = sqrt(4e9 / (2 pi x 1200 x 15.7e-12)) = 184 MHz and C_F = sqrt(15.7e-12 / (2 pi x 4e9 x 1200)) = 0.72 pF, consistent with 'around 200 MHz' and 0.6 pF.

tia_content.what: Fig 61 noise gain and I-V transfer function sketch
tia_content.other: NG = (1 + s R_F (C_IN + C_F)) / (1 + s R_F C_F); zero f_Z ~ 1/(2 pi R_F C_IN); pole f_P = 1/(2 pi R_F C_F); high-frequency NG = 1 + C_IN/C_F, meeting the open-loop curve at the GBWP-limited crossover.

tia_content.C_D_or_source_C: C_D = 10 pF drawn in Fig 63 but not included in the noise plot
tia_content.figure_or_section: p29 Eq 10, Fig 62, Fig 63; p30 text
tia_content.other: Eq 10: i_ni = sqrt(i_n^2 + (e_n/R_F)^2 + 4kT/R_F); e_no = i_ni x R_F. CURVE readings of Fig 62 total i_ni: 4.95 pA/rtHz at 1 kohm, 4.30 at 1.5 kohm, 3.95 at 2 kohm, 3.73 at 2.5 kohm, 2.90 at 10 kohm; components at 1.5 kohm: thermal 3.37, e_n/R_F 0.49, i_n 2.6 (flat line drawn at 2.6). Text: 'for R_F < 2.5 kohm, the noise performance is entirely dominated by R_F thermal noise ... at no R_F setting does the LMH6629 input noise voltage play a significant role. This noise analysis has ignored the possible noise gain increase, due to photo-diode capacitance, at higher frequencies.'

application_guidance: Compensation selection and external compensation below the minimum gain: see min_stable_gain (p20-p22, Figs 50, 51, Eq 1).

Bias-current cancellation: Rf || Rg = Rseq (non-inverting, Eq 2); for the inverting configuration a resistor Rb = Rf || (Rg + Rs) on IN+, 'no less than 25 ohm for optimum LMH6629 performance', with an optional shunt capacitor to minimise its noise. When IN+ is driven from a 0-ohm source (e.g. an op-amp output) isolate it with at least a 25-ohm series resistor (p23).

Noise model: e_ni = sqrt(e_n^2 + (i_n+ Rseq)^2 + 4kT Rseq + (i_n- (Rf||Rg))^2 + 4kT (Rf||Rg)) (Eq 3); e_ni dominated by e_n below Rseq = 15 ohm, by resistor thermal noise from 15 ohm to 2.5 kohm, by i_n above 2.5 kohm; e_n and i_n contributions equal at Rseq = 190 ohm. Example: Av = +10, -3 dB 825 MHz, Rseq = 20 ohm -> e_ni = 1.07 nV/rtHz, output noise 385 uVrms (p24-p25, Fig 57).
Capacitive load: series Riso measured at CL: 72 ohm for 4.7 pF, 40 ohm for 10 pF, 17 ohm for 33 pF (Figs 13, 14, p13).

Supply decoupling: low-inductance ceramic capacitors less than 0.5 inch from the pins, ground plane, ground plane removed near sensitive pins such as the inputs (p34). Layout: chip capacitors 1000 pF to 0.1 uF at each supply pin plus 4.7-10 uF tantalum; HD2 is strongly influenced by layout, in particular by decoupling capacitors placed between V+ and V- as close to the leads as possible; keep feedback and gain resistor traces short; terminate traces longer than 1 inch; keep resistor values low because large resistors interact with parasitic capacitance and add thermal noise (p35). Evaluation-board layers shown in Figs 69-72 (p36).

Single-supply operation with capacitive coupling (Fig 59, p27); SE-to-differential ADC driver example with COMP LO at noise gain 6 (280 MHz = 1.7 GHz / 6) and 23.4 nV/rtHz output noise (p32-p33); deBoo integrator, Sallen-Key filter and magnetic-media equalizer examples (p30, p33-p34).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Positive supply voltage -0.5 to 6.0 V; differential input voltage 3 V; input current +-10 mA; analog input voltage -0.5 V to VS; digital input voltage -0.5 V to VS; junction temperature +150 C; storage -65 to +150 C (p4 6.1). ESD: HBM +-2000 V, machine model +-200 V, CDM +-750 V (p4 6.2). No description of internal input clamp diodes; the 3 V differential limit and +-10 mA input current limit are the only input-protection data. Operating temperature -40 to +125 C.
other_notes: GBW is not a table parameter; the only values are the text figures 4 GHz (COMP HI) and 1.7 GHz (COMP LO). Fig 31 is consistent with them (DERIVED 3.8 GHz and 1.7 GHz). The COMP LO open-loop gain trace flattens above about 600 MHz (8.7 dB at 700 MHz, 7.5 dB at 970 MHz) instead of continuing at -20 dB/dec.
Output swing headroom: p1 says within 0.8 V of the rails, p33 says about 0.85 V; table TYP 0.82 V (low) and 0.81 V (high, 5 V - 4.19 V) into 100 ohm at 5 V.
Input bias current: table gives -15 uA TYP (negative = out of the device) whereas Fig 46 plots about +12 uA at 25 C; the figure plots magnitude and its typical unit differs from the table typical.

Fig 17 (+-1.5 V, 1 Vpp) red 240-ohm trace samples identically to the Fig 15 (+-2.5 V, 2 Vpp) red trace (same 390 MHz -3 dB point and same small features), suggesting reused data in the datasheet figure.

Input capacitance: only C_DIFF is marked as a simulation result; C_CM 1.7 pF is a plain typical value. The amplifier's 5.7 pF (C_CM + C_DIFF) would exceed a 1 pF photodiode capacitance in the C_IN of the datasheet TIA equations.
Typical-characteristics header (p11-p18): VS = +-2.5 V, Rf = 240 ohm, RL = 100 ohm, VO = 2 Vpp, COMP HI, Av = +10, WSON-8 and SOT-23-5 unless noted.
